_comment: Static threat guidance keyed by attack family (D10). NOT model output, and
not retrieval -- with nine families a dictionary is the honest engineering
choice and calling it RAG would oversell it.
Why this is a FILE and not knowledge the LLM supplies: the groundedness
check in the comparative study set-differences entities in the generated
report against entities in the evidence pack. Mitigation advice the model
produced from its own weights would be unverifiable by construction, and
wrong mitigation advice in a security context is worse than none. Sourcing
it here makes it checkable like every other field.
MITRE ATT&CK technique IDs are the public enterprise matrix identifiers.

scanning.description: Systematic probing of hosts or ports to map reachable services.
standard_mitigations: Rate-limit and alert on hosts contacting an unusual number of distinct destinations
Restrict east-west traffic with network segmentation
Ensure exposed services are inventoried and patched

ddos.description: Coordinated traffic volume from many sources intended to exhaust a target's capacity.
standard_mitigations: Enable upstream volumetric filtering or scrubbing
Apply per-source rate limits at the edge
Confirm autoscaling and failover behaviour for the targeted service

dos.description: Single-source traffic intended to exhaust a target service or host.
standard_mitigations: Rate-limit the source at the network edge
Review the targeted service's connection and resource limits
typical_indicators: repeated flows to one destination port

password.description: Repeated authentication attempts aimed at guessing valid credentials.
standard_mitigations: Enforce account lockout or progressive delay after failed attempts
Require multi-factor authentication on exposed services
Alert on repeated authentication failures from one source
typical_indicators: many short flows to an authentication port

injection.description: Malformed input sent to an application to alter how it parses a command or query.
standard_mitigations: Use parameterised queries and validate input server-side
Deploy a web application firewall in front of exposed applications
Review application logs for the targeted endpoint
typical_indicators: unusual payload sizes to an application port

xss.description: Script content injected into a web application so it executes in another user's browser.
standard_mitigations: Encode output contextually and validate input server-side
Set a restrictive Content-Security-Policy header
Review the affected application's request logs
typical_indicators: HTTP flows with anomalous payload characteristics

backdoor.description: Persistent unauthorised access channel into a host, often on a non-standard port.
standard_mitigations: Isolate the host and inspect it for unauthorised persistence
Block the destination and review egress filtering rules
Rotate credentials that the host had access to

ransomware.description: Malicious encryption of data, usually preceded by discovery and lateral movement.
standard_mitigations: Isolate the affected host immediately
Verify backup integrity and that backups are offline or immutable
Hunt for lateral movement from the same source

mitm.description: Traffic intercepted or relayed between two hosts that believe they communicate directly.
standard_mitigations: Enforce authenticated and encrypted transport between endpoints
Enable dynamic ARP inspection and DHCP snooping on access switches
Verify the ARP and neighbour tables of the affected hosts
typical_indicators: unexpected intermediary host between two endpoints

Benign.description: No attack behaviour indicated. Present so that false positives carry guidance too.
standard_mitigations: No action indicated; confirm against the host's normal behaviour before dismissing
